claims.claim: The literal optimized algorithm’s complexity is Θ(n+M), where M=Σ_t d(p_t) along its actual FIFO trajectory, but the ordered queue is part of the state.
claims.evidence: At a round boundary let Q be the FIFO and U the shelf with Q deleted. Initialization gives Q=D(p). Processing Q=(x_1,…,x_k) produces reverse(Q) followed by U. A decreasing-block analysis between consecutive elements of U shows that the successor-removal test enqueues exactly once each descent bottom internal to U; the old-front test enqueues exactly the descent bottoms in reverse(Q) and at its junction with U. The two classes are disjoint, so the next FIFO has no duplicates and has set D(p'). This proves the invariant inductively. The initial scan costs Θ(n), every pop, enqueue test, and linked-list move costs Θ(1), and round overhead is dominated by nonempty pops, hence total cost is Θ(n+M) with M=Σ_t|Q_t|=Σ_t d(p_t). Shelf alone is insufficient: the same reachable shelf (2,1,4,3) occurs with FIFOs (3,1) and (1,3), whose next shelves are respectively (1,3,2,4) and (3,1,2,4).
claims.witness: Initial shelf (1,4,2,3) reaches shelf (2,1,4,3) after one round with FIFO (3,1); direct initialization at shelf (2,1,4,3) gives FIFO (1,3). Their next boundary shelves differ.
claims.search_method: General local-adjacency invariant proof, supplemented by exact exhaustive boundary checks through n=9 and a search for reachable same-shelf/different-FIFO collisions.

claims.claim: There is an exact phase decomposition that isolates the unresolved cost.
claims.evidence: Let i be the largest misplaced value at a phase boundary. Values i+1,…,n form a fixed suffix, so i lies at a position s_i<i and cannot be a descent bottom. A moved item that was left of i at the beginning of a round shifts i left once upon removal and right once upon prepending, for net zero. A moved item initially right of i shifts i right exactly once. Relative side classifications cannot change before an item moves because all moves are to the front and i never moves. Thus if r_t and ℓ_t are the right- and left-side moves in round t, pos_{t+1}(i)-pos_t(i)=r_t and the round cost is r_t+ℓ_t. While i is unfixed its immediate successor is smaller and therefore moved, so r_t≥1; the phase ends exactly at position i. Consequently Σ_t r_t=i-s_i and the exact phase cost is (i-s_i)+Σ_tℓ_t. This also partitions the whole execution by successive largest misplaced values.
claims.search_method: Direct invariant and telescoping proof; the per-round and complete-phase identities were also checked at every boundary of all 409,113 permutations through n=9.

claims.claim: The parent’s Ω(n^{3/2}) lower bound and coefficient (4√2/3+o(1)) are not established for the literal optimized FIFO algorithm.
claims.evidence: The shelf-ordered transition used by the described staircase transfer is not the literal FIFO transition. For P_6=(6,1,2,3,4,5), after three rounds the literal FIFO shelf is (1,3,2,6,4,5), whereas recomputing descents in current shelf order gives (3,1,2,6,4,5). The smaller input (4,1,5,2,6,3) likewise takes 6 moves and 3 rounds literally but 5 moves and 2 rounds under the shelf-ordered transition. Hence that recurrence cannot be transferred to the literal algorithm, and no alternative argument in the draft proves either the n^{3/2} bound or its coefficient. This does not assert that the bound itself is false.
claims.witness: P_6=(6,1,2,3,4,5), with differing third boundary states (1,3,2,6,4,5) and (3,1,2,6,4,5).
claims.search_method: Exact integer trajectory comparison between the literal persistent FIFO and the autonomous shelf-order descent transition.

claims.claim: For n≤9, the exact maximum numbers of moves are 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53.
claims.evidence: Exact lexicographic enumeration covered all Σ_{n=1}^9 n!=409,113 permutations. Independent vector and predecessor/successor linked-list implementations agreed at every round boundary on the shelf, FIFO, move total, and termination. The resulting maxima were exactly 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53, and each was attained.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive enumeration of every permutation for n=1,…,9 with two exact integer-only implementations and boundary-by-boundary consistency assertions.

claims.claim: A natural twice-per-unordered-pair charging bound is false.
claims.evidence: For the stated size-4096 permutation, two independent exact linked-list implementations both produced 49,545,006 moves in 45,082 rounds. A charging rule with capacity two per unordered pair has total capacity 2·C(4096,2)=4096·4095=16,773,120. The execution exceeds that capacity by 32,771,886 moves, so such a universal charging bound is impossible. As the draft notes, this finite obstruction alone proves no asymptotic lower bound.
claims.search_method: Direct deterministic execution using independent predecessor/successor-array and std::list machines; all counts and comparisons used integer arithmetic.

claims.claim: No asymptotically tight worst-case bound is proved here; the authorized Ω(n log n)–O(n³) interval remains unresolved.
claims.evidence: The Θ(n+M) formula is trajectory-parametric and supplies no asymptotic bound on worst-case M. The phase identity leaves Σ_tℓ_t uncontrolled. Finite maxima and a single size-4096 obstruction do not establish an infinite-family rate, while the proposed n^{3/2} argument depends on a transition that is false for the literal FIFO. Therefore the draft proves neither a matching upper and lower bound nor an improvement to either authorized endpoint.
claims.search_method: Deductive dependency and target-coverage audit of every asymptotic assertion in the draft.

target_evidence: The exact target requests an asymptotically tight worst-case step complexity. The draft expressly does not provide one: its operational identity leaves worst-case M unknown, and its phase decomposition leaves the left-of-active term uncontrolled. Thus it does not fully resolve the target. However, the corrected extended-state model, exact phase identity, exhaustive finite maxima, and concrete failure of a proposed charging bound are correct and material structural progress, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate rather than NO_VALID_PROGRESS. The headline and final writeup consistently state that the Ω(n log n)–O(n³) interval remains open and label the resolution PARTIAL; claimed_resolution is therefore ACCURATE and does not overclaim coverage.
